solved.t: Was Emil the owner of the sawmill?
solved.x: No. Emil was a merchant: the Czernowitz press lists 'Maidanek Emil, Kaufmann' on a 1928 jury list and prints his donation apart from the 'Brueder Maidanek' in 1930, and the sawmill is called 'Brueder Maidanek' (1924), 'Adolf si Iosif Maidanek' (1941) and 'formerly Iosif Maidanek' (1943). Only a silent partner could still be hidden; the trade-register file in Suceava would close that.

solved.t: Who held the sawmill at the end?
solved.x: Iosif (Josef) Maidanek. Adolf died in April 1934, and the 1943 state lease notice calls the sawmill 'fosta Iosif Maidanek' (formerly Iosif Maidanek's).

solved.t: Adolf is not Emil's father Abraham
solved.x: Abraham (born 1871) died in Obodovka in 1941. Adolf died in April 1934 aged 48 (born about 1886). Two different men. The Adolf of the firm is probably a third Abraham, born 1884, son of Moses and Marie (inference, not yet proof).

conflicts.topic: Emil/Mendel birth year: family memory 1878 vs registers 1898
conflicts.ev: Q353 (R1, 10.10.2026): the 1922 Vicov marriage act P1150122 reads "laut Geburtsscheines geboren am 26. Maerz 1898" - a 1915-issued Radautz birth certificate presented at the marriage, plus the 1922 military document. Three independent register attestations of 1898 (birth register Q333, marriage act, military doc). No "Emil" birth exists in the Radautz index at all; no Maidanek birth ~1878. A different Mendel Maidanek married Winter Gitel Frime 10.6.1903 (P1120592) - disambiguation caution.
conflicts.next: Dad is the only route to where the 1878 year came from; otherwise closed.
